content: IC50/EC50 curation literature: dominant real-world errors are unit transcription errors (uM vs nM), wrong receptor/target subtype annotation, and conflating cellular vs biochemical assay types — these are not automatically detectable and require manual curation. Potency values are inherently log-scale/multi-order-of-magnitude, which is why raw-value unit mistakes are especially easy to miss (an off-by-1000 unit error still looks like a plausible number).
